9884.fact: Its name means **“the head of the ram”** in Arabic. It’s an orange giant about 66 light-years away, with a planet bigger than Jupiter circling it.

13209.fact: Really **three stars** sharing one point of light, about 166 light-years away. Its name comes from **Bharani**, one of the lunar mansions of ancient Hindu astronomy.

21421.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the follower”**, as it trails the Pleiades across the sky. This red giant marks **the Bull’s eye**, about 67 light-years away.

26451.fact: Marks the tip of **the Bull’s horn**. Its Chinese name means **“Celestial Gate”**, and it’s really a pair of stars about 440 light-years away.

18724.fact: An **eclipsing binary**: two stars that pass in front of each other every 4 days, dimming the light. Found in 1848, it was only the **third** one ever discovered.

15900.fact: As the westernmost bright star of Taurus, it got the number **1 Tauri**. It’s a yellow giant with a hidden partner that circles it every 4 and a half years.

16083.fact: Not one star but **four**. Two of them eclipse each other every 7 days, so the light dips slightly. It’s about 210 light-years away.

18907.fact: A white star about 117 light-years away that’s heading our way. In about **five million years** it will pass within roughly 18 light-years of the Sun.

37826.fact: The **closest giant star** to the Sun, just 34 light-years away. It has a planet, named **Thestias**, that’s heavier than Jupiter.

31681.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the brand”** marked on a camel’s neck. It marks one of **the Twins’ feet**, about 109 light-years away.

32246.fact: Its name comes from an Arabic phrase for an **outstretched paw**, from an old picture of a giant lion. Today it marks Castor’s outstretched leg, 860 light-years away.

32362.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the button”**. It marks one of **the Twins’ four feet**, about 59 light-years away.

35350.fact: A white star about 101 light-years away with **hidden partners**. One of them was only confirmed when **the Moon passed in front** of the star.

36962.fact: A red giant swollen to **40 times the Sun’s width**, about 253 light-years away. It drifts through space with a family of stars called the **Wolf 630 group**.

40526.fact: An orange giant about 303 light-years away that’s believed to have **a planet** of its own. It’s moving away from us at **23 km every second**.

43103.fact: A **double star**: two suns more than 3,000 times farther apart than Earth and the Sun, travelling together about 347 light-years away.

42806.fact: Its name is Latin for **“the northern donkey colt”**. With its southern partner, it seems to feed at a manger, the **Beehive star cluster** right beside it.

50583.fact: Its name means **“the forehead”**, though it sits in the Lion’s mane. A small telescope splits it into **two giant stars** orbiting each other.

54872.fact: It marks **the Lion’s back**, about 58 light-years away. This white star spins fast, its equator whirling at more than **180 km every second**.

54879.fact: A white-hot star about 165 light-years away whose light shows **extra metals**, marking it as a **chemically odd** star.

49583.fact: A **blue supergiant** nearly **20,000 times brighter** than the Sun. It only looks faint because it’s so far away, roughly 1,270 light-years.

65474.fact: Its name means **“ear of grain”**, held by the Maiden. It’s really two hot stars so close together they’re squeezed into **egg shapes**.

63608.fact: Its Latin name means **“the grape gatherer”**. Long ago, its rising before dawn told farmers it was **harvest time** for grapes.

63090.fact: A red giant about 200 light-years away. With four nearby stars, it formed an old Arabic star figure called **“the Barker”**.

72220.fact: Spins so fast, about **285 km every second**, that its middle bulges out like a **squashed ball**. It’s about 135 light-years away.

60129.fact: Really **three stars** in one, about 246 light-years away. Its name comes from the Arabic word for **“corner”**.

69701.fact: Its name is Greek for **the train of a dress**, trailing from the Maiden’s robe. It’s a pair of stars about 72 light-years away.

64238.fact: A family of **three stars** about 320 light-years away. The closest two swing around each other once every **33 years** on a long, stretched path.

72622.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the southern claw”**, from when these stars belonged to the Scorpion. Binoculars split it into **two stars**.

76470.fact: An orange giant about 31 times the Sun’s width. It was first labelled as a star of **the Scorpion**, then later **moved to Libra**.

76333.fact: Its name means **“the claws of the scorpion”**, from a time before these stars became the Scales. It’s about 163 light-years away.

85927.fact: Its name means **“the raised tail”** in Arabic. It marks **the Scorpion’s stinger**, and is really three stars in one.

78401.fact: In 2000 this star suddenly **brightened** and has flickered ever since. In 1981, Voyager 2 watched its light shine through **Saturn’s rings**.

86670.fact: One of its old names, the Sumerian **Girtab**, simply means **“scorpion”**. It’s a pair of hot stars about 480 light-years away, in the Scorpion’s tail.

81266.fact: Its Hawaiian name means to **wander from house to house**. It sits beside Antares, and was once called one of the **“arteries”** of the Scorpion’s heart.

80112.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the arteries”**, as it sits beside Antares, the Scorpion’s heart. It’s really **four stars**, one of them gently pulsing.

82514.fact: Its name comes from the Khoekhoe language of southern Africa: **“the eyes of the lion”**. It’s two stars that **eclipse each other**, and they almost touch.

82729.fact: An orange giant about 135 light-years away. Its neighbour in the sky, Zeta1, is a **supergiant 6,000 light-years** away: the two only line up by chance.

92855.fact: Two hot blue stars so close they look like one, about 225 light-years away. The Moon can pass in front of it, and **Venus did in 1981**.

89931.fact: Its name means **“the middle of the bow”**. It’s an orange giant with a tiny **white dwarf** partner, about 348 light-years away.

94141.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the town”**. It’s really **three stars**, about 510 light-years away.

89642.fact: In India, where these stars made an elephant, it marked **the elephant’s tail**. It’s a red giant about **57 times** the Sun’s width.

93864.fact: An orange giant about 122 light-years away that moves through our part of the galaxy **four times faster** than the stars around it.

93683.fact: About a million years ago this star was much closer, within **86 light-years**. Now it’s about 142 light-years away and **still drifting off**.

95168.fact: A white star that **pulses** very slightly, about once every **hour and a quarter**. It’s about 127 light-years away.

95347.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the archer’s knee”**. It may have a **dusty disc** around it, like the star Vega does.

98412.fact: Two stars whirling around each other every **2.1 days**. The bigger one shines more than **2,000 times brighter** than the Sun.

94643.fact: A family of **three stars**: two whirl around each other every 11 days, and together they circle an orange giant every **20 years**.

94820.fact: A yellow giant swollen to **24 times** the Sun’s width, about 470 light-years away. It sits near the Sun’s path, so **the Moon** sometimes covers it.

100345.fact: Probably **five stars** in one. Binoculars or a small telescope split it into **two**, and each of those is a small group of its own.

105881.fact: A yellow supergiant with a tiny **white dwarf** partner, found in 1980 by its **ultraviolet glow**. The two orbit every 6 and a half years.

102978.fact: An orange giant about 550 light-years away. It moves unusually fast and may be a **runaway star**. In China it was part of the **Celestial Farmland**.

105515.fact: A lone yellow star about 201 light-years away. In Chinese star lore it belongs to the **Twelve States**, a group named for ancient kingdoms.

101027.fact: Two stars that take **278 years** to orbit each other. About 1.6 million years ago they passed just **12 light-years** from the Sun.

109074.fact: Its name means **“the lucky star of the king”** in Arabic. It’s a rare **yellow supergiant**, about 690 light-years away.

114341.fact: Named after **Safina, the Ship**, an old Arabic star figure between Diphda and Fomalhaut. It’s an orange giant **29 times** the Sun’s width.

102618.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the swallower”**. It’s a white star with a partner, about 244 light-years away and **heading toward us**.

115438.fact: An orange giant about 163 light-years away. It’s more than **twice as heavy** as the Sun and about **14 times** as wide.

110003.fact: Its name is medieval Latin for **“the haunch”**, the hip of the Water Bearer. It’s about 191 light-years away.

115033.fact: A hot blue star spinning at more than **340 km every second**. It also **pulses** very gently, about once a day.

110672.fact: A massive star **8,300 times brighter** than the Sun, spinning so fast it **bulges** at the middle. It’s about 1,100 light-years away.

9487.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the cord”**. It marks **the knot** that ties the two Fishes together, about 157 light-years away.

7097.fact: Its old Babylonian name, **Kullat Nunu**, comes from their word for **fish**. It’s really two stars, about 350 light-years away.

116771.fact: Its Balinese name means **“battling quails”**, after a bird figure seen in Pisces. It’s a close neighbour, only about **45 light-years** away.

4906.fact: A yellow-orange giant about 182 light-years away that may have a **giant planet**, spotted in 2021. In Japan it’s called the **“Soaring Forever Star”**.

3786.fact: Its name, Waiping, is Chinese for the **Outer Fence**, which hid a pigsty in the old star maps. It’s a lone orange giant about 300 light-years away.

113889.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the mouth of the fish”**, from the same words as Fomalhaut. It’s a blue-white star about 410 light-years away.

5586.fact: An orange giant about 169 light-years away. It now burns **helium** in its core, a later stage in a star’s life than our Sun has reached.

5571.fact: An orange giant about 384 light-years away. It’s only about **380 million years old**, but at three times the Sun’s mass it has aged fast.

6193.fact: This white star is **98% of the way** through the main part of its life. Next, it will swell into a **giant**. It’s about 308 light-years away.

115738.fact: It marks a corner of **the Circlet**, a ring of stars in Pisces. Its surface is oddly rich in **strontium, chromium and silicon**.

24436.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“foot”**, and it marks Orion’s. This blue supergiant is at least **60,000 times** brighter than the Sun.

25336.fact: Its name is Latin for **“female warrior”**. At about 250 light-years, it’s the **closest** of the seven stars that make Orion’s famous shape.

26727.fact: The brightest **O-type star** in our sky, the hottest kind of star. It marks the east end of **Orion’s Belt** and is really three stars.

25930.fact: Sits almost exactly on the **celestial equator**, so it rises due east and sets due west. This Belt star is really **five stars** in one.

25281.fact: Its Arabic name means **“the sword of the giant”**, though that name now belongs to Saiph. It’s a family of **several stars**, about 1,000 light-years away.

22549.fact: Two hot stars that orbit each other every **9.5 days**, about 1,050 light-years away. The bigger one shines nearly **20,000 times** brighter than the Sun.

22957.fact: An orange giant about 186 light-years away. At around **5.4 billion years old**, it’s **older than our Sun**.

22509.fact: Part of **Orion’s shield**. This white star spins at over **260 km every second**, making its middle bulge out. It’s about 224 light-years away.

29038.fact: Two stars on a stretched-out orbit, circling each other every **131 days**. The main one is a **hot blue star**, about 520 light-years away.

23123.fact: An orange giant swollen to about **88 times** the Sun’s width. It shines around **2,200 times** brighter than the Sun, from about 950 light-years away.

22845.fact: A young star, just **100 million years old**, about 116 light-years away. It’s circled by a cold ring of **dust**, a bit like our own Kuiper Belt.

24010.fact: About three million years ago it passed within **69 light-years** of us. Now it’s about 340 light-years away and **still moving off**.

54061.fact: One of **the Pointers**: draw a line from Merak through it and keep going to reach **Polaris**, the North Star. It’s about 123 light-years away.

65378.fact: Sharp eyes can see its faint neighbour **Alcor**, an old eyesight test. A telescope shows Mizar itself is double, and it’s really **four stars**.

58001.fact: It marks a corner of **the Dipper’s bowl**. Like most Dipper stars, it travels through space with a star family called the **Ursa Major moving group**.

11767.fact: It sits less than 1 degree from **the north pole of the sky**, so it barely moves all night. It’s really **three stars**, led by a yellow supergiant.

75097.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the calf”**. With Kochab it forms the **Guardians of the Pole**, circling Polaris all night.

77055.fact: It **pulses** in brightness every **15.8 hours**, and it’s also eclipsed now and then. It’s a white star about 369 light-years away.

79822.fact: A yellow-white star about 98 light-years away and **coming closer**. It’s spinning fast, at about **85 km every second**.

3179.fact: It and Caph are so close in brightness that **which one wins** depends on how you measure. It’s an **orange giant** marking the Queen’s chest.

6686.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“knee”**, the Queen’s knee. It’s an **eclipsing binary** about 99 light-years away.

102098.fact: Its name means **“tail”** in Arabic, and it marks the Swan’s. This blue supergiant is at least **55,000 times** brighter than the Sun.

102488.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the wing”**, and it sits on the Swan’s wing. It’s an orange giant about 73 light-years away.

95947.fact: A small telescope splits it into a **gold star and a blue star**, one of the prettiest sights in the sky. It marks **the Swan’s beak**.

95853.fact: A white star spinning at about **240 km every second**. It’s heading our way and in about 783,000 years will be within **92 light-years**.

98110.fact: An orange giant on **the Swan’s long neck**, halfway between Sadr and Albireo. It’s about 139 light-years away and now burns **helium** in its core.

62434.fact: Its name may come from the Latin for **“actor”**. In ancient Greek times it could be seen much farther north, and they counted it as part of **Centaurus**.

59747.fact: Its name comes from the **Mursi people** of Ethiopia. It’s the faintest of **the Southern Cross’s** four main stars, about 345 light-years away.

677.fact: Shared by two pictures: the Princess’s head and a corner of **the Great Square of Pegasus**. Its main star is oddly rich in **mercury**.

3092.fact: A family of **three stars**, about 106 light-years away and drifting closer. In Chinese star lore it’s part of a figure called **the Legs**.

113726.fact: It was the head of **the Complete Horse**, an old Arabic star figure. It’s a blue-white giant system about 690 light-years away.

4436.fact: It sits halfway between Mirach and the **Andromeda Galaxy**, so it’s a handy signpost for finding it. It’s really **two stars**, 122 light-years away.

116805.fact: It has a **giant planet** many times heavier than Jupiter, one of the first ever **photographed directly**. It’s about 168 light-years away.

116631.fact: One of the **steadiest** stars the Hipparcos satellite measured, barely flickering at all. Its name means **“the head of the camel”**.

2912.fact: A pair of hot blue stars that orbit every **143 days**, with a **third star** farther out. They’re about 580 light-years away.

3881.fact: Just over a degree from the **Andromeda Galaxy** in our sky. It’s two stars orbiting every **4.3 days**, about 560 light-years away.

51172.fact: The brightest star in the Air Pump, yet it has **no proper name**. It’s an orange giant about **41 times** the Sun’s width.

53502.fact: An orange giant about 208 light-years away and **3.3 billion years old**. It now burns **helium** in its core.

81065.fact: An orange giant about 153 light-years away that gives off strong **X-rays**. It’s about **2.7 billion years** old.

80047.fact: A red giant that **pulses** in brightness every few months. Its neighbour in the sky, **Delta2**, is an orange giant, and the two may travel together.

97278.fact: Its name comes from Persian for **“the scale beam”**, a line it makes with Altair and Alshain. It’s an orange giant about 395 light-years away.

99473.fact: Named after **Antinous**, an old constellation now folded into the Eagle. It’s really two stars, about 286 light-years away and **heading toward us**.

93805.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the two ostriches”**, shared with Iota Aquilae. Its hidden partner star was found with the **Very Large Telescope**.

97804.fact: A **Cepheid**, a star that swells and shrinks, changing brightness on a steady beat. Its name, Pagru, is Akkadian for **“the dead man”**.

85258.fact: A young **supergiant** swollen to about **141 times** the Sun’s size. It’s only around 50 million years old, and about 710 light-years away.

85267.fact: A huge, hot star blazing about **120,000 times** brighter than the Sun. Its path through space traces back to the **Scorpius** region of the sky.

82363.fact: An orange giant that spins so slowly one turn takes **more than 11 years**. It’s about 305 light-years away.

24608.fact: Its name means **“little goat”** in Latin. It’s really **four stars**: two yellow giants plus a pair of small red dwarfs, about 43 light-years away.

28380.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the wrist”** of the Charioteer. It’s a pair of stars about 166 light-years away.

23416.fact: Every **27 years** it dims for nearly two years as a **huge dark disc** passes in front of it. It’s around 3,300 light-years away.

23453.fact: Its name is an **old misspelling** of Sadatoni. It’s an orange giant and a hot blue star that **eclipse** each other every 2.7 years.

69673.fact: Its name means **“guardian of the bear”** in Greek, as it follows the Great Bear. It’s about 37 light-years away and **7 billion years old**.

67927.fact: A near neighbour at about **37 light-years**. Since 1943 astronomers have used its light as a **standard** for sorting other stars.

74666.fact: Binoculars or a small telescope show a faint **companion star**. It marks the east edge of the Herdsman’s **kite shape**, about 121 light-years away.

71053.fact: In Chinese star lore it’s part of the **Celestial Lance**. It’s a lone orange star about 164 light-years away, **coming closer**.

70497.fact: Its name is Latin for **“the first donkey colt”**. It’s a near neighbour, just **47 light-years** away, in the Herdsman’s raised hand.

67275.fact: One of the first stars found to have a **planet**, announced in 1996. It also has a small **red dwarf** partner, and it’s about 51 light-years away.

21770.fact: A close neighbour, just **66 light-years** away. It has a small **red dwarf** partner, and a ring of dust circles the main star.

23522.fact: A yellow supergiant about 840 light-years away. It spins **unusually fast** for such an old, swollen star.

22783.fact: A blue supergiant nearly **38 times** heavier than the Sun. It’s thought to be a **runaway star**, flung out of the star cluster NGC 1502.

23040.fact: A family of stars: the main one has a hidden partner that whirls around it every **3.9 days**. They’re about 370 light-years away.

17959.fact: It spins at more than **200 km every second**, so its middle bulges out about **17% wider** than its poles. It’s about 386 light-years away.

61317.fact: A near twin of **our Sun**, just 28 light-years away. With Cor Caroli, it forms **the southern dog** of the Hunting Dogs.

32349.fact: Its name comes from Greek for **“glowing”** or **“scorching”**. Just 8.6 light-years away, it has a tiny **white dwarf** partner nicknamed the Pup.

34444.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“weight”**. This yellow-white supergiant is about **1,600 light-years** away.

35904.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the maiden”**. It’s a blue supergiant so far away its light set out around **2,000 years ago**.

30122.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the solitary ones”**. It’s a pair of stars about 362 light-years away, moving away from us.

33160.fact: It marks **the Dog’s nose**. This orange giant is about **10 billion years old**, more than twice the age of our Solar System.

33347.fact: A blue-white supergiant about 3,100 light-years away. It’s just **15 million years old**, a baby next to our 4.6-billion-year-old Sun.

36188.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the bleary-eyed one”**. This hot blue-white star sits close to **Procyon** in the sky.

45238.fact: The brightest star of the **Diamond Cross**. Edmond Halley once made it the top star of his own constellation, **Charles’s Oak**, now dropped.

41037.fact: Part of the **False Cross**, a pattern so like the Southern Cross that it has fooled navigators. It’s really two stars, about 610 light-years away.

45556.fact: Its name comes from Greek for **“little shield”**. It’s part of the **False Cross**, a pattern often mistaken for the Southern Cross.

31685.fact: About 3.6 million years ago it passed within **27 light-years** of the Sun. It’s a hot blue giant ringed by a **disc of gas** we see edge-on.

51576.fact: A hot star spinning at about **325 km every second**, wrapped in glowing gas. It belongs to the **Southern Pleiades** star cluster.

38827.fact: About **seven times** heavier than the Sun and only 40 million years old. It may have an **unseen partner** tugging on it.

54463.fact: A rare **yellow hypergiant**, one of the biggest and brightest kinds of star there is. Its light wobbles slightly over many months.

54301.fact: A yellow giant about 383 light-years away. It’s almost **4 times** the Sun’s mass and has swollen to **21 times** its width.

71681.fact: The second star of **Alpha Centauri**, the nearest star system to us at about 4.4 light-years. It circles its brighter twin every **79 years**.

61932.fact: Two stars so close a telescope barely splits them, about 130 light-years away. They may share a wider family with **Tau Centauri**.

71352.fact: It spins so fast it turns once in **less than a day**, throwing off a ring of gas. It’s about 306 light-years away.

59196.fact: A hot **shell star** that spins so fast it throws gas out into a disc. Its brightness wobbles a little, and it’s about 410 light-years away.

73334.fact: A family of **three stars**. The inner two take **58 years** to orbit each other, and we see their path almost edge-on.

67472.fact: A textbook **“Be” star**: a hot star wrapped in a disc of glowing gas. It marks **the Centaur’s right side**, about 510 light-years away.

60823.fact: A **helium-rich** star, the heaviest kind of chemically odd star. It’s about **7 times** the Sun’s mass and 412 light-years away.

105199.fact: Its name means **“the right arm”** in Arabic. Around the year 7500, Earth’s slow wobble will make it our **North Star**.

106032.fact: The original **Beta Cephei star**: a whole class of pulsing stars is named after it. It’s really three stars, about 690 light-years away.

102422.fact: Just **47 light-years** away. With Alderamin and Alfirk it was one of **“the Stars of the Flock”** in old Arabic star lore.

110991.fact: The star that gave **Cepheids** their name: it brightens and dims every 5.4 days. Stars like it help astronomers **measure distances** across space.

101093.fact: Two stars that orbit each other every **2.5 years**, about 139 light-years away. The main one is a white star rich in **metals**.

3419.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the second frog”**. This orange giant is easy to spot because it sits alone in a **dark patch** of sky.

5364.fact: An orange giant about 121 light-years away that astronomers use as a **standard** for sorting stars. It has **two planets**.

8102.fact: One of the closest Sun-like stars, just under **12 light-years** away. From there, our Sun would look like a star in **Boötes**.

6537.fact: An orange giant about 112 light-years away, roughly **2.2 billion years old**. It now burns **helium** in its core.

12387.fact: It sits less than a degree from the galaxy **M77**, which needs a telescope to see. It’s a hot blue star about 650 light-years away.

11484.fact: Astronomers use it as a **standard star** to check their light measurements. About 2.7 million years ago it was closer, at **128 light-years**.

12093.fact: A pair of stars about 340 light-years away, part of a family called the **Ursa Major stream** drifting together through space.

51839.fact: An orange giant swollen to about **78 times** the Sun’s width and shining **864 times** brighter. It’s about 444 light-years away.

58484.fact: John Herschel saw it was **double** in 1836. In 2016, astronomers found one of those stars is double too, making **three**.

74824.fact: A white star about 100 light-years away, nearly **twice** the Sun’s mass. It’s somewhere between **370 and 500 million** years old.

26634.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“ring dove”**, a name once used for the constellation Cygnus. It’s a hot blue-white star about 261 light-years away.

30277.fact: Before the Dove existed, it was called **3 Canis Majoris**. It’s two stars on a long, stretched orbit, and may be a **runaway**.

28328.fact: An orange giant about **36 times** the Sun’s width and nearly **5 times** as heavy. It’s about 441 light-years away.

64241.fact: Really **two stars**, 58 light-years away. Their orbit is **edge-on** to us, so they seem to slide back and forth in a straight line.

94160.fact: An orange giant whose light shows unusually strong **cyanogen**, a molecule made of carbon and nitrogen. It’s about 470 light-years away.

93825.fact: Two nearly identical stars that take about **122 years** to orbit each other. They’re close neighbours, just **56 light-years** away.

90982.fact: A yellow giant about 4 times the Sun’s mass that has swollen to **29 times** its width. It’s about 530 light-years away.

93174.fact: Two stars so close they **touch**, sharing one outer layer. Its light dips and rises every **14 hours**, the brightest star of this kind in our sky.

75695.fact: Two stars that take about **10.5 years** to orbit each other, about 112 light-years away. In Chinese star lore it’s part of the **Rope Binding**.

76127.fact: A pair of young stars, just **85 million years old**, about 375 light-years away. A telescope shows the fainter one right beside the bright one.

77512.fact: In India, the Northern Crown is called **Matrichakra, “the circle”**, and this star now carries that name. It’s a yellow giant that gently **varies**.

59803.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“wing of the crow”**, and on modern charts it marks the Crow’s **left wing**. It’s about 154 light-years away.

60965.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the crow”**, after the whole constellation. It’s a white star about **87 light-years** away.

59199.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“tent”**, and another old name means **“beak of the crow”**. It’s a near neighbour, about 49 light-years away.

55705.fact: It sits at **the centre of the Cup**. A small telescope splits it into **two stars**, about 87 light-years away.

54682.fact: Two stars that orbit every **6 years**, about 9 times farther apart than Earth and the Sun. They’re about 317 light-years away.

57283.fact: A pair of stars so close in our sky that only a big telescope splits them. Its brightness stays remarkably **steady**, from about 343 light-years away.

101769.fact: Its name is **a joke**: read Rotanev backwards and you get **Venator**, the Latin surname of astronomer Niccolò Cacciatore.

101421.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the dolphin”**. It’s a hot blue-white giant about 330 light-years away, **heading our way**.

21281.fact: Two stars on a stretched orbit that brings them close every **12 years**. The bigger one is unusually rich in **silicon**.

19893.fact: The star that gave a whole class of pulsing stars its name, the **Gamma Doradus variables**. Its light wobbles in rhythms of **13 to 18 hours**.

27890.fact: An orange giant about **eight billion years old**, much older than our Sun. It’s just 89 light-years away.

87833.fact: In 1728, James Bradley used it to show that **Earth moves**. In 1.5 million years it will pass close by and become the **brightest star** in our sky.

85670.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **the serpent’s head**. A faint dwarf partner circles it about once every **4,000 years**.

83895.fact: Its old Arabic name means **“the wolf”** or **“the hyena”**. It’s really two stars, about 330 light-years away.

89937.fact: Two Sun-like stars that orbit each other every **281 days**. At about 27 light-years, it’s one of the **200 closest** stars to us.

87585.fact: Its name is a garbled copy of the Latin for **“snout”**, as Ptolemy placed it on **the Dragon’s jaw**. It’s about 113 light-years away.

97433.fact: With three neighbours it formed **“the Goat”** in old Arabic star lore. In China it’s a star of the **Celestial Kitchen**.

78527.fact: Two stars that whirl around each other every **3 days**, about 69 light-years away. Astronomers first found it was double back in **1899**.

85829.fact: Its name, Alawaidh, is Arabic for **“the camel mothers”**: four stars guarding a newborn calf. Binoculars show it as **two white stars** side by side.

104858.fact: It was the head of **Nekhet, the Giant**, an ancient Egyptian star figure. It’s really two Sun-like stars, about 60 light-years away.

7588.fact: Its name means **“end of the river”** in Arabic. It spins so fast it’s **squashed**, much wider around its middle than from pole to pole.

13847.fact: Its name means **“end of the river”**, but a copyist misread “rn” as “m”. A small telescope splits it in two, and it’s really **three stars**.

17378.fact: Rana means **“frog”** in Latin, a name borrowed by mistake from Diphda. It’s a close neighbour, just **30 light-years** away.

10602.fact: A hot blue-white star spinning so fast its middle is **17% wider** than its poles. It may have a faint yellow **partner** far off.

15474.fact: A red giant **103 times** the Sun’s width that slowly **flickers** in brightness. It’s about 300 light-years away.

21393.fact: A yellow giant about 211 light-years away, three times the Sun’s mass. Over the centuries its name has been spelled **Theemim** and even **Beemin**.

21444.fact: If it were only **33 light-years** away, it would outshine Sirius as the brightest star in our sky. It **pulses** in at least 14 rhythms at once.

22109.fact: Two stars that **eclipse** each other every 7.4 days, and the main one also gently **pulses**. It’s about 520 light-years away.

14146.fact: A white star about 89 light-years away, spinning at over **130 km every second**. It may have a **disc of dust** around it, like Vega.

17874.fact: A yellow giant about 218 light-years away. It drifts through space with the **Ursa Major moving group**, the star family of the Big Dipper.

12770.fact: Officially part of Cetus, but often drawn as part of **the River**. It’s two stars that circle each other every **7.5 years** in an almost perfect circle.

16611.fact: Two stars whirling around each other every **6.2 days**, closer together than Mercury is to the Sun. They’re about 293 light-years away.

17593.fact: A red giant about **77 times** the Sun’s width, shining over 1,100 times brighter. Its brightness changes **slowly and irregularly**.

13147.fact: A yellow giant about 177 light-years away. Close by in the sky is **NGC 1049**, a star cluster that belongs to **another galaxy**.

109268.fact: Its name means **“the bright one”** in Arabic. It’s one of the **58 stars** navigators use to find their way, about 101 light-years away.

108085.fact: Its name means **“the tail”**: it was once the tail of **the Southern Fish**, before the Crane constellation was made.

110997.fact: A yellow giant **24 times** the Sun’s width that slowly varies in brightness. Its sky neighbour, **Delta2**, is a red giant.

111043.fact: A red giant that **pulses** in several rhythms, the strongest every **33 days**. With the yellow Delta1 beside it, it makes a naked-eye pair.

109908.fact: Two stars that take **19 years** to orbit each other, about 275 light-years away. The main one is a yellow giant **9 times** the Sun’s width.

84345.fact: Its name means **“the kneeler’s head”**. Old maps drew Hercules **upside down**, so his head sits at the bottom of the figure.

84379.fact: A pair of stars about 75 light-years away. Three more stars sit close to it in the sky, but they **only look** like part of the group.

86974.fact: A family of **four stars** just 27 light-years away. The main one is a lot like **our Sun**, but older, and starting to swell into a giant.

87933.fact: A yellow giant about 137 light-years away, twice the Sun’s mass. It may belong to the **Sirius stream**, stars drifting through space together.

88794.fact: Its old name **Masym**, Arabic for “the wrist”, was later handed to Lambda Herculis. It’s a bluish-white giant, **355 times** brighter than the Sun.

79992.fact: Its name, **Asuusiha**, comes from the **Manchu** language. It’s a blue-white star whose brightness gently varies, about 307 light-years away.

85112.fact: A telescope shows **two stars** side by side, and the brighter one is itself a **close pair**. All of them are hot, blue-white stars.

79101.fact: A **mercury-manganese star**, with odd amounts of those metals on its surface. A partner star circles it every **565 days**.

19747.fact: An orange giant about 118 light-years away and **3.5 billion years** old. It’s the brightest star of **the Clock**, a constellation named in the 1750s.

46390.fact: Its name means **“the solitary one”** in Arabic, as no other bright stars sit near it. It’s an orange giant about 177 light-years away.

43813.fact: Part of **the Snake’s head**. Its neighbour Delta Hydrae is only about **13 light-years** from it, and the two may travel together.

68895.fact: An orange giant about 101 light-years away whose light shows unusually **weak cyanogen**. It also spins **very slowly**.

56343.fact: Flamsteed listed it as **19 Crateris**, back when Hydra and Crater were drawn together. It’s a giant about 130 light-years away.

51069.fact: Just 1.8 degrees away is **the Ghost of Jupiter**, a glowing cloud left by a dying star. Mu Hydrae itself is an orange giant **45 times** the Sun’s width.

47431.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“knot”**, after a group of four stars in the Snake’s coils. It’s an orange giant about 263 light-years away.

42313.fact: A family of **three stars**: two orbit each other every **200 days**, with a third farther out. They’re about 160 light-years away.

42799.fact: The faintest of the five stars that make **the Snake’s head**. It’s a hot blue star about **seven times** the Sun’s mass, roughly 590 light-years away.

72571.fact: An orange giant about **8 billion years old** and poor in iron, about 290 light-years away. Flamsteed first listed it as **6 Librae**.

2021.fact: The nearest easy-to-see star to **the south pole of the sky**. Around 150 BC it was the **southern pole star**. It’s just 24 light-years away.

17678.fact: A red giant **62 times** the Sun’s width, yet with about the **same mass** as the Sun. Its brightness slowly pulses.

12394.fact: A young star, just **133 million years** old, about 152 light-years away. It travels with a star family called the **Tucana-Horologium group**.

101772.fact: An orange giant about 100 light-years away, 1.6 billion years old. It may have **two small red dwarf** companions.

105319.fact: A telescope splits it into **two stars**. The fainter one is itself a pair that orbits every **30 years**. It’s about 99 light-years away.

102333.fact: A member of the **Octans association**, a group of stars only **30 to 50 million years** old. It’s about 79 light-years away.

109937.fact: An orange giant swollen to about **69 times** the Sun’s width and **1,450 times** brighter. It’s about 680 light-years away.

110538.fact: Its name Alsamaka means **“the fish”**: it belonged to an old Arabic star figure called **“the smaller fish”**. It’s about 170 light-years away.

109754.fact: An orange giant about 570 light-years away. Double star catalogues list it with a **faint companion** close beside it.

110351.fact: Two hot blue stars whirling around each other every **2.6 days**, too close for any telescope to split. They’re about 550 light-years away.

53229.fact: Its name is Latin for **“the chief”**. It should have been labelled alpha, but the letter was **accidentally left out** of an old star catalogue.

49593.fact: It spins at least **155 km every second** and gently **pulses** in brightness. It’s about 92 light-years away and may have a ring of dust.

51056.fact: A white star about 233 light-years away. It has finished the main part of its life and is on its way to becoming a **red giant**.

25606.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“quenching their thirst”**. In China it was part of a star group called, believe it or not, **the Toilet**.

24305.fact: A blue-white star about 170 light-years away with unusual amounts of **mercury and manganese** in its outer layers.

27072.fact: A near neighbour at **29 light-years**. Binoculars show its partner, AK Leporis, a star whose **starspots** make it flicker.

27654.fact: An old orange giant, about **10.7 billion years** old, more than twice the Sun’s age. It’s about 114 light-years away.

24327.fact: A telescope shows a faint **partner star** right beside it. The main star is nearly **five times** the Sun’s mass, about 730 light-years away.

71860.fact: One of the **nearest stars** that could one day explode as a **supernova**. It’s a hot blue giant about 460 light-years away.

76297.fact: Two stars orbit every **2.8 days**. The hotter one heats the side of its partner, so the light **flickers** slightly as they turn.

75264.fact: A family of several stars about 510 light-years away. Its two closest stars are only known from the way their light **shifts back and forth**.

78384.fact: Its two main stars take about **27,000 years** to orbit each other. They belong to a nearby family of young, hot stars.

77634.fact: A family of **three stars**: a mercury-rich star, a metal-rich star and a small **red dwarf**. Their star family is only about 11 million years old.

74911.fact: A system of **three stars and a brown dwarf**, a “failed star” too small to shine. Two of the stars take **772 years** to orbit each other.

45860.fact: The **only star** in the Lynx with a Greek letter. It’s a red giant about **58 times** the Sun’s width, roughly 220 light-years away.

44248.fact: It sits in Lynx, but its name says Ursa Major: **Flamsteed** put it in the **wrong constellation**. It’s two stars just 53 light-years away.

33449.fact: A telescope splits it into **two yellowish stars**. They take **262 years** to orbit each other, about 178 light-years away.

36145.fact: A white star about 274 light-years away. It spins slowly for its type, which makes the lines in its light look extra **sharp**.

93194.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“turtle”**, because fine harps were once made from **tortoiseshell**. It’s about 620 light-years away.

92791.fact: Its name comes from a Chinese star group for **water clocks**. It began as a hot blue star and is now a cool, swollen **red giant**.

91926.fact: Part of the famous **Double Double**: sharp eyes see two stars here, and a telescope splits each of those **in two again**.

25918.fact: An orange giant about **10.6 billion years** old, more than twice the Sun’s age, yet with nearly the same mass. It’s about 102 light-years away.

105140.fact: Its name honours **Globus Aerostaticus**, an old constellation shaped like a **hot-air balloon** that’s no longer used. It’s about 166 light-years away.

102831.fact: A yellow giant about 395 light-years away, over 3 times the Sun’s mass. A faint star beside it is **only a line-of-sight** neighbour, not a partner.

37447.fact: Though labelled alpha, it’s **not the brightest** star in the Unicorn. It’s a yellow-orange giant about 146 light-years away.

34769.fact: It sits half a degree south of **the celestial equator**. About 7.3 million years ago it passed within **88 light-years** of the Sun.

30419.fact: A handy signpost for finding the **Rosette Nebula**, a huge flower-shaped cloud. A telescope shows a yellow-white **partner star** beside it.

32578.fact: Halfway between **Orion’s Belt and Procyon**. It’s an orange giant with a little extra **barium** and a hidden partner that orbits every 4.8 years.

61585.fact: A hot blue-white star nearly **nine times** the Sun’s mass, shining about **4,300 times** brighter. It’s about 315 light-years away.

63613.fact: An orange giant with a hidden partner, about 91 light-years away. Johann Bayer gave it its Greek letter in his famous **1603 star atlas**.

61199.fact: Its brightness rises and falls every **2.7 days** as it slowly pulses. It also spins so fast that its middle **bulges** out.

80000.fact: An orange giant about 138 light-years away, **heading our way** at 29 km every second. It’s about twice the Sun’s mass.

78639.fact: The **Gamma Normid** meteor shower seems to come from a spot near this star. It’s a yellow giant about 219 light-years away.

107089.fact: It’s two stars, and a **planet** circles the main one in the space **between them**, a puzzle for astronomers. It’s about 74 light-years away.

70638.fact: If you stood on **Saturn**, this would be your **south pole star**. It’s an orange giant about the same age as our Sun.

84012.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the preceding one”**. It’s really **two white stars**, about 88 light-years away.

79593.fact: Yed comes from Arabic for **“hand”**. With Yed Posterior it forms the Serpent Bearer’s **left hand**, gripping the snake.

83000.fact: One of the **reference stars** astronomers have used since 1943 to sort other stars by type. It’s an orange giant about 92 light-years away.

84970.fact: It marks the Serpent Bearer’s **right foot**, right beside where **Kepler’s Star** exploded in 1604. It’s really three stars.

80569.fact: A hot blue star spinning fast and wrapped in a **disc of gas**, which makes its brightness wander. It’s about 500 light-years away.

80894.fact: A yellow giant about 244 light-years away, **heading toward us** at about 33 km every second.

80473.fact: It sits at the heart of the **Rho Ophiuchi cloud**, one of the most colourful sights in space photos. The star itself is a family of **hot blue stars**.

102395.fact: A white star about 135 light-years away. It travels with the **Ursa Major moving group**, the same star family as most of the Big Dipper.

86929.fact: An orange **bright giant** about **33 times** the Sun’s width, shining 469 times brighter. It’s about 350 light-years away.

91792.fact: An orange giant about 215 light-years away. It travels with the **Hyades Supercluster**, a stream of stars moving through space together.

92609.fact: A hot, fast-spinning star wrapped in a **disc of gas**. Now and then it **brightens**, from about 1,400 light-years away.

90098.fact: Its faint partner was found in 1894 by **Walter Gale**, an Australian amateur astronomer. The system holds **three stars**.

113881.fact: It marks **the upper right corner** of the Great Square of Pegasus. This red giant’s name may come from Arabic for **“the upper arm”**.

1067.fact: It marks **the southeast corner** of the Great Square of Pegasus. It’s really two stars, about 470 light-years away.

112029.fact: Its name is said to mean **“man of high spirit”**. In Chinese star lore it belongs to a group called **Thunder and Lightning**.

109427.fact: A white star 92 light-years away, spinning at over **130 km every second**. It’s about **448 million years** old.

112440.fact: Its name, Ligong, is Chinese for a **temporary palace** where an emperor could rest. It’s a yellow giant about **28 times** the Sun’s width.

87108.fact: Its name is Marshallese and refers to a kind of **spiny shellfish**. With Beta Ophiuchi it forms the Serpent Bearer’s **right shoulder**.

112447.fact: A yellow-white star just 53 light-years away, in **the Horse’s neck**. A small **red dwarf** travels through space alongside it.

18246.fact: A **supergiant** star, far bigger than the Sun. It once shared the old name Atik, **“the collarbone of the Pleiades”**, which now officially belongs to Omicron Persei.

14328.fact: Every **14.6 years** one of its two stars passes in front of the other, dimming the pair for about two weeks. The **Perseid meteors** seem to come from nearby.

14354.fact: The third of **the Gorgons**, sisters from the legend of Perseus. It’s a red giant that changes brightness in rhythms of 50 to 250 days.

13268.fact: An orange supergiant about 1,000 light-years away. Its name **Miram** turned up in the 1900s, and **nobody knows** where it came from.

17448.fact: Near it in the sky lies **IC 348**, a young star cluster. Its name Atik comes from Arabic for **“the collarbone of the Pleiades”**.

19343.fact: A hot, fast-spinning star with a wobbly **disc of gas** around its middle. Its brightness flickers with a **5-day** rhythm.

8068.fact: Flamsteed, following Ptolemy, placed it in Andromeda as **54 Andromedae**. In Chinese star lore it belongs to **Heaven’s Great General**.

12777.fact: One of the closest naked-eye stars, just **37 light-years** away. A small **red dwarf** circles it at about 250 times the Earth-Sun distance.

19167.fact: It spins so fast its middle bulges out about **16%**. Its light hints at bright patches caused by a **magnetic field**.

14817.fact: The fourth of **the Gorgons**, sisters from the legend of Perseus. It’s an orange giant about 288 light-years away.

2081.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the phoenix”**. Older Arab astronomers saw a boat here, and called it **“the bright one of the skiff”**.

6867.fact: Two stars orbit every **194 days**, so close they’re pulled into **egg shapes**, making the light rise and fall.

7083.fact: A yellow giant about 142 light-years away and **2.3 billion years** old. It now burns **helium** in its core.

32607.fact: If you stood on **Mercury**, this would be your **south pole star**. It’s really two stars that orbit every 3 years and 7 months.

15863.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“elbow”**. It sits in the middle of the **Alpha Persei Cluster**, a lovely spray of stars in binoculars.

27530.fact: An orange giant about 185 light-years away. Its width, about **11 times** the Sun’s, was measured directly by **linking telescopes** together.

111954.fact: A hot star spinning at about **216 km every second**, not far from the speed that would make it **fly apart**. It’s about 550 light-years away.

111188.fact: Its Chinese name means **“Celestial Rope”**, for the ropes used to pitch tents. It’s part of a pair of stars, about 143 light-years away.

112948.fact: A family of **three stars**, about 216 light-years away. The main one is rich in rare metals like **europium** and strontium.

39429.fact: One of the **hottest** stars you can see, over **500,000 times** more powerful than the Sun. It’s a runaway, likely flung out when a partner exploded.

39757.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“little shield”**. Just 63 light-years away, it’s the model for a group of odd, metal-rich stars called **Rho Puppis stars**.

37229.fact: Not a kappa at all: its letter is a **Latin k**, given when the old ship constellation **Argo** was split up. It’s two stars that only look close.

38835.fact: A yellow-white bright giant with a surprising amount of **lithium**, which it seems to have made recently. It’s about 522 light-years away.

36917.fact: A family of **five stars**, including a faint **white dwarf**. The main one is a hot blue-white star about 222 light-years away.

42515.fact: A yellow giant that spins **unusually fast** for its age. One idea is that it **swallowed a giant planet**, which sped it up.

19780.fact: Its name **Rhombus** is an old name for the Reticle constellation itself. It’s a yellow giant about 160 light-years away.

19921.fact: An orange star with a **planet**, confirmed in 2000, and a tiny **white dwarf** partner. It’s about 60 light-years away.

98337.fact: Its name **Telum** is Latin for **“dart”**, an old name for the Arrow itself. It’s a red giant about 58 times the Sun’s width.

96757.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“arrow”**. Despite being alpha, it’s **not the brightest** star in the Arrow. It’s a yellow bright giant about 430 light-years away.

4577.fact: A hot blue-white giant about 780 light-years away. Its brightness wobbles slightly as **patches** on its spinning surface turn into view.

115102.fact: An orange giant about 182 light-years away. At **4 to 6 billion years** old, it’s around the same age as our Sun.

91117.fact: Flamsteed didn’t count the Shield as a constellation, so he called this star **1 Aquilae**. Its Chinese name means **“Celestial Cap”**.

90595.fact: It’s heading our way at 41 km a second. In about **2.35 million years** it may pass 20 light-years away and become the **brightest star** in our sky.

77622.fact: A white star just 70 light-years away whose light is **chemically odd**: different parts of it match **three different star types** at once.

78072.fact: A star a bit bigger than our Sun, just **36 light-years** away, in **the Serpent’s head**.

76852.fact: Two matching white stars so close they were first found by their **wobble**. Two fainter stars sit farther out, about 190 light-years from us.

48437.fact: Two white stars so close together only a large telescope can split them. They take about **78 years** to orbit each other.

90568.fact: An orange giant about 122 light-years away. It’s only **40% heavier** than the Sun, but **8 times** as wide.

10064.fact: With Alpha Trianguli it was called **“the Scale Beam”** and **“the Two Friends”** in Arabic. It’s really two stars, about 127 light-years away.

10670.fact: Its name comes from **Apdu, the Bird**, an ancient Egyptian star figure. It’s a white star about 112 light-years away.

77952.fact: In Australia’s Wardaman culture its name, **Jirradella**, means **“rainbow sign”**. It’s a close neighbour at about 40 light-years.

110130.fact: An orange giant **37 times** the Sun’s width, with a hidden partner that circles it every **11.5 years**.

1599.fact: A near **twin of our Sun** just 28 light-years away, and one of the **steadiest** stars the Hipparcos satellite ever measured.

118322.fact: It spins at around **300 km every second**, so its middle bulges out about **36%**. It’s a hot blue-white star about 373 light-years away.

54539.fact: In Chinese star lore it stands alone as **the Royals**, inside the Purple Forbidden enclosure. It’s an orange giant about 140 light-years away.

44127.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the third leap of the gazelle”**, a pair of stars on the Bear’s paw. It’s just 47 light-years away.

77070.fact: Its name comes from Arabic for **“the snake’s neck”**, and it was also called **Cor Serpentis**, “the heart of the serpent”. It’s an orange giant 74 light-years away.

41704.fact: Its name comes from Latin for **“snout”**: it marks the Bear’s nose. In 2012 a **planet** was found circling it.

55219.fact: An orange giant **60 times** the Sun’s width, about 399 light-years away. With Alula Australis it marks the Bear’s paw.

46733.fact: A yellow-white star about 78 light-years away, nearly **twice** the Sun’s mass. A faint **partner star** travels alongside it.

48319.fact: It **pulses** quickly, about every 3 hours, and spins once every **1.2 days**. It’s about 120 light-years away.

48402.fact: Two matching white stars that take about **105 years** to orbit each other. In 4.7 million years they’ll be at their closest to us, about 370 light-years.

45941.fact: Part of the **False Cross**, a pattern that has fooled navigators hunting for the Southern Cross. It’s a hot blue star about 572 light-years away.

48774.fact: Its old name, **Tseen Ke**, comes from Chinese for **“star chart”**. It’s a blue-white supergiant about 28,000 times brighter than the Sun.

34481.fact: It sits about 9 degrees from the **Large Magellanic Cloud**, a neighbouring galaxy. A small telescope shows its **yellow-white partner**.

44382.fact: Two near-twin stars far too close for a telescope to split by eye. They belong to the **Sirius supercluster**, stars drifting through space together.

95771.fact: Its name is Latin for **“goose”**: the constellation was once **the little fox with the goose**. It’s a red giant about 291 light-years away.

97886.fact: A blue giant with a partner star that takes about **615 years** to orbit it. It’s about 339 light-years away and **heading our way**.

94703.fact: In 1983 the asteroid **Pallas** passed in front of it, and observers at **130 places** timed it to map the asteroid’s shape.

50191.fact: A white star about 103 light-years away with a cold **ring of dust** around it. It travels with the **Argus Association**, a family of young stars.

16870.fact: An orange giant about 247 light-years away. About 3.8 million years ago it passed closer to us, within **141 light-years**.

96465.fact: A hot blue-white star about 190 light-years away, rich in **strontium and iron**. Its small orange **partner** gives off X-rays.

8903.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the two signs”**, because thousands of years ago it helped mark the start of spring. It’s really two stars circling each other every 107 days.

8832.fact: Robert Hooke spotted that it was **two stars** back in 1664, and a small telescope still splits the pair today. They sit about 166 light-years away.

25428.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the butting”**, as in a bull’s horns, and it marks the tip of one. It sits so near Auriga that it was once counted in **both constellations**.

20894.fact: Its name is the Maya word for **a small bird**. It belongs to the Hyades, the V-shaped cluster that forms the Bull’s face, and is really **four stars** in two pairs.

20889.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“eye”**, marking one of the Bull’s eyes. This orange giant has a giant planet named **Amateru** circling it, about 146 light-years away.

20205.fact: Its name means **“first of the Hyades”**. It marks the tip of the V that forms the Bull’s face, near the heart of the closest star cluster to the Sun.

20455.fact: Its name means **“second of the Hyades”**. It’s an orange giant with partner stars, part of the cluster that shapes the Bull’s face, about 156 light-years away.

16852.fact: A Sun-like star just **45 light-years** away and older than our Sun. It was once the brightest star of a forgotten constellation, **George’s Harp**.

36850.fact: It looks like one star, but it’s really **six stars** in three pairs, all circling each other. They sit about 50 light-years away.

30343.fact: A **red giant** over 100 times wider than the Sun, about 230 light-years away. Its name comes from an old Arabic word whose meaning has been lost.

29655.fact: Its name is Greek for **“forward foot”**, and it marks a twin’s foot. It’s a red giant that slowly changes brightness, with **two partner stars**.

35550.fact: Its name means **“middle”** in Arabic. In 1930, Clyde Tombaugh discovered **Pluto** just half a degree from this star.

34088.fact: A **Cepheid**, a star that swells and shrinks on a steady beat, about every 10 days. Astronomers use stars like it as **measuring sticks** for distances in space.

34693.fact: An orange giant 30 times wider than the Sun, with a **brown dwarf** circling it every 305 days. Brown dwarfs are too big to be planets but too small to be true stars.

42911.fact: Its name is Latin for **“southern donkey colt”**. It sits beside the **Beehive Cluster** and so close to the Sun’s path that the Moon sometimes covers it.

44066.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the claws”**, marking the Crab’s pincer. It’s a fast-spinning white star with a faint companion.

49669.fact: Its name is Latin for **“little king”**, and it marks the Lion’s heart. It spins once every 16 hours, so fast that it’s **squashed** wider at its middle.

57632.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“tail of the lion”**, and that’s exactly what it marks. It’s a white star just **36 light-years** away.

47908.fact: Its name means **“the southern star of the Lion’s head”**. This yellow giant is about 21 times wider than the Sun and sits about 247 light-years away.

50335.fact: Its Arabic name means **“the lock of hair”**, for its spot in the Lion’s mane. Since 1943, astronomers have used its light as a **standard** for sorting other stars.

48455.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“north lion’s head”**. In 2014, astronomers found a **planet** circling this orange giant, about 124 light-years away.

61941.fact: Named after a **Roman goddess of prophecy**. It’s two nearly identical stars that circle each other once every **169 years**, about 38 light-years away.

66249.fact: Nobody knows where its name came from: it first showed up in a **1951 star atlas**. A small, faint partner star was found circling it in 2010.

57757.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“corner of the barking dog”**. It sits near the Sun’s path, so planets sometimes cover it. Venus will next do it in the year **2210**.

71957.fact: Its old Arabic name means **“the foot of the barking dog”**. It sits near the celestial equator, so it can be seen from **almost anywhere on Earth**.

57380.fact: A **red giant** 54 times wider than the Sun, even though it has a little less mass. It marks the western tip of Virgo, about 331 light-years away.

68520.fact: A white star nearly **twice the Sun’s mass**, spinning so fast its surface races around at 186 km per second or more. It sits about 225 light-years away.

74785.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the northern claw”**, from when these stars were the Scorpion’s claws. Old stargazers called it the only **greenish star** you can see by eye.

73714.fact: Its name is Latin for **“arm”**. This red giant used to be called Gamma Scorpii, until new constellation borders in 1930 **moved it into Libra**.

76600.fact: Three or four stars in one. The closest two whirl around each other in just **3.3 days**, tugging so hard the main star pulses like a **heartbeat**.

80763.fact: Its name means **“rival of Mars”**, for its red colour. Put this supergiant where the Sun is and it would reach out to the **asteroid belt**.

86228.fact: Its name may come from Persian for **“arrowhead”**. Spinning fast has **squashed** this giant: about 35 Suns wide at its waist but only 26 from pole to pole.

82396.fact: Its name comes from the Wardaman people of northern Australia and means **“clear sighting”**. It’s an orange giant only about 64 light-years away.

78820.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the scorpion”**. A small telescope splits it in two, but it’s really **six stars**, all bound together.

78265.fact: Its name comes from the Chinese star group **“Room”**. Its two hot blue stars race around each other in just **1.6 days**, about 590 light-years away.

87073.fact: A rare **yellow-white supergiant**, shining about 35,000 times brighter than the Sun. Its light set out about 1,900 years ago, in the days of the Roman Empire.

84143.fact: The most southern Scorpius star with a Greek letter. In 2018 the Gaia spacecraft showed it has a **partner star**, both about 73 light-years away.

90185.fact: Its name means **“southern part of the bow”**, and it’s the Archer’s brightest star. It spins so fast that it’s **squashed**, much wider at its middle.

93506.fact: Its name comes from a Latin word meaning **“armpit”**. It’s really **three stars** together, about 88 light-years away.

90496.fact: It marks the **top of the Archer’s bow**. Venus last passed in front of it in 1984, and before that Mercury did in 1865.

88635.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“arrowhead”**, and it marks the tip of the Archer’s arrow. The **centre of our galaxy** lies just a few degrees from it.

92041.fact: A blue-white giant with a hidden partner. In 2017, astronomers confirmed a smaller star circling it **about once a year**, about 239 light-years away.

93085.fact: An orange giant 27 times wider than the Sun, about 390 light-years away. It wobbles slightly as it moves, a sign of an **unseen partner** star.

89341.fact: A **blue supergiant** about 5,000 light-years away, much farther than most stars you can see by eye. It has several partner stars around it.

95241.fact: A blue-white star nearly at the end of its calm, steady life. It has a **partner star** that a small telescope can show, about 310 light-years away.

98032.fact: An orange giant with a faint partner first seen directly in **2014** by a giant telescope in Chile. The partner is over **4,000 times fainter**.

95176.fact: One of only **four known** star pairs where one star has lost almost all its hydrogen. Its partner is pulling gas off it, about 1,800 light-years away.

98066.fact: Two stars in a very stretched orbit, circling each other every **4.7 years**. Its name once covered a little group of **four stars** at the Archer’s back.

92761.fact: Its name means **“eye of the archer”** in Arabic. It’s really **three stars**, about 1,100 light-years away, sitting almost exactly on the Sun’s path.

107556.fact: Its name means **“the tail of the goat”**. It’s two stars that pass in front of each other, so it dims a little about **once a day**.

106985.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“bearer of good news”**. Its light shows odd amounts of metals like **strontium and europium**.

104139.fact: Formally named Udang, after a **shrimp** constellation from Bali. It sits so close to the Sun’s path that the Sun nearly covers it each **February**.

102485.fact: A yellow-white star about 48 light-years away. Around **467,000 years ago** it passed within 20 light-years of the Sun.

100027.fact: It and Algedi look like a **naked-eye pair**, but they aren’t related. This yellow supergiant is about 800 light-years away, many times farther than its partner.

106278.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“luck of lucks”**. This yellow supergiant is about 48 times wider than the Sun and roughly 540 light-years away.

110960.fact: It sits at the centre of the **Water Jar**, a little Y of stars. It’s two stars circling each other once every **587 years**, about 95 light-years away.

112961.fact: Its name, Shatabhisha, means **“a hundred physicians”**, one of the lunar mansions of ancient Hindu astronomy. In 2014 **Venus** passed right in front of this red giant.

110395.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“luck of the tents”**, one of a group of stars once pictured as tents. It’s a white star with a close partner, about 164 light-years away.

111497.fact: The **Eta Aquariid meteor shower** is named after it, since the meteors seem to stream from near here each May. They’re crumbs from **Halley’s Comet**.

109139.fact: A blue-white star with a hidden partner that circles it about every **40 days**. The partner was first detected in 2009 and seen directly in 2016.

103045.fact: Two stars so close they look like one even in big telescopes, circling every **2.4 years**. Its light shows unusual amounts of **europium**.

116901.fact: A golden giant about 32 times wider than the Sun, roughly 840 light-years away. It grew this big in only **135 million years**.

114971.fact: A **visitor** from another part of the Milky Way, passing us at about 153 km per second. In 2021 a **giant planet** was found circling it.

118268.fact: Its name, Pili, is Chinese for **“thunderbolt”**. It marks where the Fish’s tail begins, just past the Circlet, about 100 light-years away.

8198.fact: It sits near the Sun’s path, and on **13 May 2027** Venus will pass in front of it, as seen over Newfoundland. It’s an orange giant about 280 light-years away.

115830.fact: An orange giant about 11 times wider than the Sun, now burning **helium** in its core. It sits about 149 light-years away.

7884.fact: Before 1930 it belonged to Cetus as **51 Ceti**. This orange giant has a **white dwarf** partner that long ago sprinkled it with heavy elements.

116928.fact: It forms the southeast corner of the **Circlet**, the western Fish’s ring of stars. It travels through space with the **Big Dipper’s family** of stars.

8833.fact: An orange giant with a hidden partner that circles it every **4.6 years**. The partner was found in 1901 by studying its light.

5742.fact: It’s really **four stars**. Its two main pairs swing around each other every 20 and a half years on a very **stretched orbit**.

7007.fact: An orange giant 37 times wider than the Sun, about 304 light-years away. At about **5.6 billion years old**, it’s older than our Sun.

117245.fact: A **carbon star**, one of the reddest stars you can see by eye. Binoculars show off its deep red glow, about 800 light-years away.

27989.fact: A red supergiant so big that, in place of the Sun, it would swallow **Mars’s orbit**. In 2019 and 2020 it faded oddly, an event called the **Great Dimming**.

26311.fact: The middle star of **Orion’s Belt**. Its name means **“string of pearls”**, and this blue supergiant shines about 270,000 times brighter than the Sun.

27366.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“sword of the giant”**, though it marks Orion’s knee. This blue supergiant is even **hotter** at its surface than Rigel.

22449.fact: At just **26 light-years** away, it’s the nearest bright star in Orion. Its name is Arabic for **“the endurer”**, and it sits in the shield Orion holds.

26207.fact: Its name means **“the shining one”**, and it marks Orion’s head. It’s so hot that most of its light is **ultraviolet**, which our eyes can’t see.

22797.fact: Two stars so close they **stretch each other into egg shapes**, circling every 3.7 days. Their light set out about 1,300 years ago.

28614.fact: It looks like one star, but it’s really **four**: two tight pairs, each closer together than Mercury is to the Sun.

27913.fact: A near twin of our Sun, just **28 light-years** away, but much younger. It marks the tip of Orion’s **raised club**.

29426.fact: A young blue-white star, only about **32 million years old**, with a partner that circles it every 45 days. It sits high above Betelgeuse, about 610 light-years away.

28716.fact: It looks faint only because it’s so far away and dimmed by dust. This **blue supergiant** actually gives off more light than **Rigel**.

23607.fact: A **magnetic star** with patches of extra silicon and chromium on its surface. As it turns, every 4.6 days, its brightness wavers slightly.

62956.fact: The handle star closest to the Dipper’s bowl. It’s one of the **57 navigation stars** sailors used to find their way at sea.

67301.fact: It marks the end of the Dipper’s handle and is a **baby star**, only about 6 million years old. Unlike most Dipper stars, it isn’t part of their travelling family.

53910.fact: One of the two **Pointer stars**. Draw a line from it through Dubhe and keep going, and you’ll reach **Polaris**, the North Star.

59774.fact: The faintest Big Dipper star, joining the handle to the bowl. It spins once every **3.1 hours** and has a **dusty disc** around it.

72607.fact: With Pherkad, it’s one of the **“Guardians of the Pole”** circling Polaris. In 2014 a **giant planet**, about 6 times Jupiter’s mass, was announced around it.

82080.fact: Two stars that **eclipse** each other every 39.5 days. Canadian astronomer **J. S. Plaskett** first worked out their orbit in 1910.

85822.fact: Its name comes from the Turkish word for **“star”**. It’s the second star in the Little Bear’s tail, and it spins so fast that it **bulges** at its middle.

4427.fact: Apollo astronauts nicknamed it **Navi**, “Ivan” backwards, for Gus Grissom. Its official name, Tiansi, is an old Chinese star group: **four horses** pulling a chariot.

746.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“palm”**, as in the palm of a hand. This white star pulses, brightening and dimming slightly every **2.5 hours**.

8886.fact: A hot blue-white star about **3,000 times brighter** than the Sun. Its name was probably a copying mistake for Seginus, a star in Boötes.

100453.fact: Its name means **“chest”** in Arabic, marking the Swan’s chest where the **Northern Cross** meets. This supergiant is about 1,800 light-years away.

97165.fact: Part of the **Northern Cross**, on one of the Swan’s wings. It’s really **three stars** travelling together, about 165 light-years away.

104732.fact: A yellow giant with a tiny **white dwarf** partner circling it every 17.8 years. Long ago, that partner dusted it with heavy elements like **barium**.

94779.fact: It marks the tip of the Swan’s left wing. The small **Kappa Cygnid meteor shower** seems to stream from a spot just north of it.

60718.fact: It’s on the flags of Australia and New Zealand, and on Brazil’s flag it stands for **São Paulo**. It’s really a family of **seven stars**.

61084.fact: The **nearest red giant** of its kind, about 89 light-years away. It marks the top of the Southern Cross.

5447.fact: Stargazers hop from it to find the **Andromeda Galaxy**. A faint galaxy nicknamed **“Mirach’s Ghost”** hides right beside it.

9640.fact: A small telescope splits it into a **golden star and a blue one**, one of the prettiest pairs in the sky. The blue one is itself several stars.

7607.fact: An orange giant about 21 times wider than the Sun, roughly 170 light-years away. Johann Bayer drew it in **Perseus**, as Upsilon Persei.

116584.fact: In 2025 it was named **Udkadua**, after a Sumerian star figure, “the storm demon with the gaping mouth”. This star marked the demon’s **heel**.

3693.fact: An orange giant pulled into an **egg shape** by a partner that circles it every 17.7 days. Astronomers have even pictured **starspots** on its surface.

5434.fact: A **Be star**: it spins fast and throws off a flat disc of hot gas around its middle. It has a partner star, about 720 light-years away.

3031.fact: A **speedster**, rushing toward us at 84 km per second on a looping path through the galaxy. It has much **less iron** than the Sun.

4463.fact: Two yellow giants circling each other every **116 days**. A special telescope on Mount Wilson in California first split the pair in the early 1990s.

117221.fact: Three stars in one, led by a yellow **supergiant**. Its light set out about **2,000 years** ago, so you’re seeing it as it was in Roman times.

46515.fact: An orange giant more than **50 times wider** than the Sun. The light reaching you tonight set out roughly 700 years ago.

72370.fact: The brightest star of the **Bird of Paradise**. It’s so far south that from much of the southern hemisphere it **never sets**.

81852.fact: An orange giant about 11 times wider than the Sun, roughly 156 light-years away. It’s drifting **toward us** at about 30 km per second.

97649.fact: Just **17 light-years** away, it spins once in under eight hours, so fast that it’s **flattened** at the poles. It’s a corner of the Summer Triangle.

93747.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“eagle”**, and it marks the Eagle’s tail. It spins so fast that it’s **squashed**, much wider at its middle.

95501.fact: Two stars circling every **3.4 years**, too close to split in any telescope. In about 335,000 years they’ll pass within 25 light-years of the Sun.

98036.fact: Its name comes from a Persian phrase meaning **“the scale beam”**. In about **207,000 years** it will pass within 27 light-years of the Sun.

85792.fact: A **Be star** spinning so fast, around 375 km per second, that it throws off a disc of gas. It sits about 270 light-years away.

83081.fact: An orange giant **114 times wider** than the Sun, glowing about 3,800 times brighter. Some astronomers think it’s really a supergiant.

85727.fact: A fast-spinning blue-white star with a hidden partner found by the **Gaia** spacecraft. They loop around each other every 2.5 years.

83153.fact: An orange giant almost **30 times wider** than the Sun, about 368 light-years away. It’s moving away from us at about 24 km per second.

28360.fact: Its name means **“shoulder of the rein holder”**. In about a million years it will come close enough to become the **brightest star** in our night sky.

23015.fact: Its name first appeared in a **1951 star atlas**, and nobody knows where it came from. Under an older name, it was on the **astrolabe** Chaucer described in 1391.

23767.fact: Its name is Latin for **“kid”**, a young goat. It’s one of the **Kids**, a little pair of stars beside Capella, the she-goat.

28358.fact: The **Delta Aurigid meteor shower** in October is named after it. It has a hidden partner that circles it every **3.5 years**.

72105.fact: Struve named it **Pulcherrima**, Latin for “loveliest”, for its colourful pair: a small telescope shows an **orange star beside a blue-white one**.

71075.fact: It marks the Herdsman’s **left shoulder**. This white star gently pulses, and it’s moving toward us at about 32 km per second.

73555.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the Herdsman”**, the whole constellation, and it marks his **head**. It’s a yellow giant about 235 light-years away.

71795.fact: **William Herschel** discovered in 1796 that it was two stars. The two are near twins, about 180 light-years away.

69732.fact: The first known of a rare kind of star, the **Lambda Boötis stars**, which have strangely few metals. It also pulses every **33 minutes**.

69483.fact: Its name is Latin for **“third donkey colt”**. A small telescope splits it into two, and the brighter one pulses about every **65 minutes**.

23595.fact: An orange giant with a fainter **yellow partner** just beside it, a pair you need a telescope to split. They sit about 185 light-years away.

16228.fact: It sits inside a faint dusty cloud that **glows by reflecting its light**. A near-twin **blue supergiant** lies just half a degree to the south.

17884.fact: A red giant about **250 times wider** than the Sun, swelling and fading a little at random. Its light set out around 960 years ago.

33694.fact: An orange giant about 19 times wider than the Sun, roughly 191 light-years away and heading **toward us** at almost 30 km per second.

29997.fact: A white star spinning so fast that it **bulges** at its middle. In about 485,000 years it will make its **closest pass** by the Sun.

63121.fact: The fainter of the two stars that make up **Cor Caroli**, “Charles’s Heart”. A small telescope easily splits it from its brighter partner.

33579.fact: About **4.7 million years ago** it was the brightest star in our night sky, far brighter than Sirius is now. It’s a blue giant about 420 light-years away.

30324.fact: Its name means **“the herald”**, because it rises just before Sirius. It pulses gently, brightening and dimming every **six hours**.

33977.fact: A **blue supergiant** about 65 times wider than the Sun and more than 3,000 light-years away. It’s only about **7 million years old**.

33856.fact: The Boorong people of Victoria, Australia, saw it as **Nganurganity**, a lizard ancestor who fights the Moon, flanked by his **two wives**.

34045.fact: Nobody knows for sure why such a faint star got the **“gamma”** label. It’s a blue-white giant about 430 light-years away.

37279.fact: Its name means **“before the dog”**, as it rises just ahead of Sirius. Only 11.5 light-years away, it has a tiny **white dwarf** partner.

30438.fact: The **second-brightest star** in the night sky, after Sirius. It’s so bright and easy to find that spacecraft use it to **navigate**.

39953.fact: Apollo astronauts named it **Regor**, “Roger” backwards, for astronaut Roger Chaffee. It holds the closest and brightest **Wolf-Rayet star**, a rare blazing-hot type.

42913.fact: The **brightest known eclipsing star**: two stars that take turns passing in front of each other. The Galileo probe at Jupiter helped spot it dimming.

52419.fact: The brightest star of the **Southern Pleiades** cluster. Its two stars orbit in just **2.2 days**, the fastest known for such heavy stars.

50099.fact: The most southern bright star of Carina, part of the **Diamond Cross**. It spins fast and wears a **disc of gas** around its middle.

50371.fact: An orange bright giant about **nine times the Sun’s mass**, big enough that it may one day explode as a **supernova**. It flickers slightly in brightness.

53253.fact: An orange star about 95 light-years away, swelling into a **giant** now that the hydrogen in its core is running out. It’s about 7 times wider than the Sun.

54751.fact: A white **supergiant** about 9,000 light-years away, yet you can still see it by eye. It’s the brightest star in a cluster near the **Carina Nebula**.

68702.fact: With Alpha Centauri, it forms the **Pointers**, which lead to the Southern Cross. Its old name Agena may come from the Latin for **“knees”**.

68933.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“shoulder”**, the Centaur’s shoulder. It may be a **visitor** from the outer Milky Way, just passing through.

66657.fact: A hot blue giant about **16,000 times brighter** than the Sun, roughly 430 light-years away. Its brightness wavers slightly as the star gently pulses.

68002.fact: Two hot stars that whirl around each other in just over **eight days**, about 382 light-years away. The main one spins very fast.

65109.fact: A white star about 59 light-years away. It has twice the Sun’s mass but only about a **third of its metals**.

67464.fact: Two stars too close for any telescope to split. We only know the partner is there from its **tug** on the main star, about 437 light-years away.

55425.fact: The main star spins at around 340 km per second, so it **bulges 22% wider** at its middle than from pole to pole. It has a partner star.

59449.fact: A young blue-white star, only about **24 million years old**. It belongs to the nearest family of big, hot stars to the Sun.

116727.fact: In about **1,100 years** it will take over from Polaris as the North Star. A giant planet named **Tadmor** circles it.

109492.fact: An orange supergiant about **172 times wider** than the Sun, roughly 1,000 light-years away. It marks the left shoulder of **King Cepheus**.

112724.fact: In about **3,000 years** it will be one of the closest stars to the sky’s north pole. For now it’s an orange giant about 115 light-years away.

109857.fact: A yellow-white star that pulses every **59 minutes**. A **dusty debris disc** circles it, about 85 light-years from us.

107259.fact: **William Herschel** called its colour “a very fine deep garnet”. It’s one of the biggest stars known, about **760 times wider** than the Sun.

14135.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“nostril”**, the sea monster’s nose. This red giant is about **100 times wider** than the Sun.

12706.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the cut-short hand”**. It’s really **three stars**, about 80 light-years away.

1562.fact: Its name means **“the northern tail of the sea monster”** in Arabic. It’s an orange giant about 279 light-years away.

8645.fact: Its name means **“belly of the sea monster”** in Arabic. This orange giant has a close partner star, about 253 light-years away.

12828.fact: It sits right by the Sun’s path, so the **Moon** sometimes passes in front of it. It’s a pair of stars about 87 light-years away.
