13954.fact: This star first carried the name **Menkar**, which today usually means Alpha Ceti. It’s a blue-white giant about 446 light-years away.

40702.fact: In about **666,000 years** it will pass within 47 light-years of the Sun. It’s a yellow-white star with unusually little **iron**.

60000.fact: A blue-white star spinning so fast it **bulges** at its middle. The TESS space telescope caught it **slowly pulsing**.

71908.fact: It **pulses every 6.8 minutes**, and its surface has odd layers of metals like chromium. It has an orange dwarf partner, 54 light-years away.

75323.fact: Two stars on a very **stretched orbit** that takes about 258 years. Herschel spotted that it was a pair back in 1835.

27628.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“weight”**. About **107,000 years ago** it swept within 2 light-years of the star Beta Pictoris, maybe stirring up its dust disc.

25859.fact: An orange giant 25 times wider than the Sun. It’s moving unusually fast for its neighbourhood, so it may be a **runaway star**.

64394.fact: A near **twin of our Sun**, just 30 light-years away and younger. Despite its “beta” label, it’s a bit **brighter** than the constellation’s alpha star.

60742.fact: An orange giant about 12 times wider than the Sun, roughly 167 light-years away. It helps mark **Queen Berenice’s hair**, which she offered to the gods.

94114.fact: Its name is Latin for **“southern”**: the full old name meant the southern Alphecca, after the bright gem of the **Northern Crown**.

94005.fact: An orange giant about 11 times wider than the Sun, now burning **helium** in its core. It’s about 185 light-years away.

93542.fact: A young blue-white star, only about **76 million years old**, spinning at around 300 km per second. It’s about 179 light-years away.

76267.fact: Its name means **“the bright one of the broken ring”**, the jewel of the Northern Crown. It’s two stars that **eclipse** each other every 17.4 days.

76952.fact: In 2026 it was named **Baltesha**, after an ancient Sumerian star figure, the “Asterism of Dignity”. It’s two stars about 146 light-years away.

78159.fact: An orange giant nearly **24 times wider** than the Sun, with a giant **planet** at least six times Jupiter’s mass circling it.

78493.fact: Its surface shows strange amounts of **mercury and manganese**. A hidden partner swings around it every 35.5 days on a stretched orbit.

61359.fact: Its name first appeared in a **1951 star atlas**, and nobody knows what it means. It’s a yellow bright giant about 146 light-years away.

59316.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“beak”**, the Crow’s beak. This orange giant was once a hot **blue-white star** before it swelled to 57 times the Sun’s width.

55282.fact: The brightest star in **the Cup**, even though it got the “delta” label. This orange giant is about 20 times wider than the Sun.

53740.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“the cup”**. This orange giant is speeding **away from us** at about 47 km per second.

56633.fact: Astronomers use it as a **standard star** for measuring the brightness of others. It spins so fast that it bulges at its middle.

55687.fact: An orange giant almost **45 times wider** than the Sun, yet with about the **same mass** as our Sun.

101958.fact: Its name is **Nicolaus backwards**. Astronomer Niccolò Cacciatore sneaked it into a star catalogue in 1814 as a little **joke** naming it after himself.

102281.fact: Two nearly identical stars that orbit each other every **40.6 days**, and **both** of them pulse in brightness.

26069.fact: A **Cepheid** that swells and shrinks every 9.8 days, its width changing by about 4 Suns. **Hubble** measured its distance, about 1,040 light-years.

27100.fact: It’s the **Moon’s south pole star**: stand at the Moon’s south pole and it sits almost straight overhead. It spins so fast it bulges at its middle.

23693.fact: A Sun-like star just **38 light-years** away, a bit hotter and much younger than our Sun. A faint partner shares its path, far out from it.

80331.fact: In an old Arabic star story, it and Zeta Draconis were **“the two wolves”**, lying in wait for a young camel. It’s a yellow giant 92 light-years away.

94376.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the goat”**. It’s a yellow giant about 98 light-years away, near the Dragon’s head.

75458.fact: In 2002 a giant planet was found circling it, later named **Hypatia** after the ancient scholar of Alexandria. It’s about 101 light-years away.

68756.fact: Over 4,000 years ago, while Egyptians were building pyramids, it was the **North Star**. Its name means **“large snake”** in Arabic.

56211.fact: A red giant **70 times wider** than the Sun, about 333 light-years away. Its brightness slowly rises and falls over about **three years**.

61281.fact: From about 1800 to 1000 BC it was the **closest naked-eye star** to the sky’s north pole. It’s a blue giant wrapped in a disc of gas.

89908.fact: Three stars in one. The main star has such **strong magnetic fields** that its brightness shifts every 1.7 days as it turns.

104987.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“a piece of the horse”**, fitting for the Little Horse. It’s a yellow giant and a white star circling every 99 days.

104521.fact: A strange star with odd amounts of **strontium, chromium and europium**. It quivers in brightness about **every 12 minutes**.

23875.fact: Its name means the **“footstool”** of Orion, since it sits right by the hunter’s foot. It’s a white giant about 89 light-years away.

18543.fact: Astronomers use it as a **standard** for its kind of red giant. Data from the **Gaia** spacecraft revealed a tiny partner star sharing its path.

20042.fact: Two nearly identical stars that orbit each other every **five days**, both rich in **mercury and manganese**.

9007.fact: A yellow star about 58 light-years away, with a faint partner you need a telescope to see. Its slight flickering might come from a **hidden third star**.

16537.fact: Named for **Rán**, the Norse goddess of the sea. Just **10.5 light-years** away, it’s young, with dusty rings and at least one planet.

13701.fact: Its name came from a **copying mistake**: medieval scribes miswrote an Arabic word in a name meaning **“the ostrich nest”**.

20535.fact: An orange giant about **54 times wider** than the Sun, glowing over 400 times brighter. It sits about 296 light-years away.

19587.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“eggs”**, and its neighbour Keid means **“eggshells”**. It pulses gently, about 122 light-years away.

12486.fact: An orange giant 11 times wider than the Sun, yet only a little heavier. It’s about **3.5 billion years old**, roughly 151 light-years away.

17651.fact: A yellow-white star about **57 light-years** away, a little bigger and brighter than our Sun. It’s quiet, with no magnetic storms seen.

11407.fact: A blue-white star about **1,175 times brighter** than the Sun, roughly 510 light-years away. It’s about 93 million years old.

15510.fact: A Sun-like star just **20 light-years** away, with **three planets** and a dusty disc circling it.

12843.fact: About **305,000 years ago** it passed within 30 light-years of the Sun. Its two stars circle each other every 958 days.

14879.fact: Only **46 light-years** away, it’s really **three stars**. Flamsteed once counted it as part of Eridanus, as 12 Eridani.

9677.fact: A blue-white star with patches of extra **silicon**. As it turns, once every 1.9 days, its brightness flickers slightly.

112122.fact: Its name comes from the **Tuamotu** islands of French Polynesia. This red giant is about **150 times wider** than the Sun.

112623.fact: A blue-white star spinning so fast it **bulges** 18% at its middle. A disc of **dust** seems to circle it.

113638.fact: An orange giant 9 times wider than the Sun. It has much **less iron** than our Sun.

109111.fact: About **805,000 years ago** it came within 183 light-years of us. Now this orange giant, 22 times wider than the Sun, is moving away.

80816.fact: Its name is Greek for **“club bearer”**, meaning Hercules himself. It looks like one star, but it’s really **two**.

81693.fact: Two stars just **35 light-years** away, circling each other every **34.5 years**. A good telescope can split them.

84380.fact: The northeast corner of the **Keystone**, the four-star box at Hercules’s middle. This orange giant is about **64 times wider** than the Sun.

81833.fact: Part of the **Keystone**. Follow the line from it toward Zeta Herculis and you’ll find **M13**, one of the finest star clusters in the sky.

80170.fact: A fast-spinning white giant with a **hidden partner** star, known only from the way its light shifts. It’s about 193 light-years away.

87808.fact: An orange giant **82 times wider** than the Sun. Its brightness wanders up and down every week or so, and it’s heading toward us.

83207.fact: Astronomers still disagree about whether it’s **two stars or three**. It sits about 155 light-years away and is moving toward us.

81126.fact: Two stars circling each other every **7.4 years**. The brighter one spins so fast that it **bulges** 18% at its middle.

77760.fact: A Sun-like star about 52 light-years away, but about **9 billion years old**, roughly twice the Sun’s age. Its surface is unusually calm.

13884.fact: A white giant spinning so fast that it **bulges** at its middle. It sits about 295 light-years away in the **Clock** constellation.

64962.fact: Named **Naga** in 2026, after the serpent that people in Bali see in Hydra. It marks the **snake’s tail**.

52943.fact: An orange giant 21 times wider than the Sun, near Hydra’s border with the Cup. It gives off **X-rays**, about 137 light-years away.

43109.fact: A family of **three or four stars** in the Water Snake’s head. Its name comes from an ancient Indian star group meaning **“the embrace”**.

49841.fact: An orange giant about 109 light-years away. The spiral galaxy **NGC 3145** sits right beside it in the sky.

45336.fact: Its tiny **white dwarf** partner was found in 1998 from the **X-rays** it gives off. That dwarf was once a bigger star than the main one is now.

48356.fact: A yellow giant with a **brown dwarf**, at least 49 times Jupiter’s mass, circling it. The companion was announced in 2005.

57936.fact: It used to be called **28 Crateris**, until the 1930 borders moved it into Hydra. John Herschel found that it’s a **double star** in 1834.

43234.fact: One of the stars in the **Water Snake’s head**. It’s a fast-spinning white star about 354 light-years away, with a faint companion.

42402.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for the Hydra’s **“nostril”**. It’s an orange giant about 28 times wider than the Sun, roughly 370 light-years away.

9236.fact: Sometimes called the **Head of Hydrus**, the little Water Snake. You can find it just southeast of bright **Achernar**.

11001.fact: A white star spinning so fast it **bulges** at its middle. It’s about 140 light-years away and roughly 209 million years old.

8928.fact: One of the **steadiest stars known**, barely changing in brightness. In 2005 a giant **planet** was found circling it.

103227.fact: An orange bright giant about **56 times wider** than the Sun. It has both a hot outer layer and cool winds, a rare mix called a **hybrid giant**.

108431.fact: Two stars circling each other every **12.2 years**. South African astronomer W. S. Finsen first worked out their orbit.

111169.fact: The brightest star of **Lacerta**. Its name, Stellio, is the other name **Hevelius** gave the Lizard when he created the constellation. It’s about 100 light-years away.

111022.fact: A cool **supergiant** over **400 times wider** than the Sun, paired with a hot blue-white star. Their light set out about 2,200 years ago.

111944.fact: An orange giant 30 times wider than the Sun, now burning **helium** in its core. It’s about 350 light-years away.

111104.fact: A heavy blue-white star, about **12 times the Sun’s mass**, with a partner circling every 880 days. Its light set out about 1,900 years ago.

110609.fact: A **blue supergiant** about 2,600 light-years away. It has probably already been a **red supergiant** once, and is now heating up again.

51233.fact: The only star in Leo Minor with a **Greek letter**, yet only the second brightest. It’s two stars circling each other every **39 years**.

46952.fact: A yellow giant with a very **active surface**, which makes its brightness waver slightly. It’s about 191 light-years away.

25985.fact: Its name is Arabic for **“hare”**, fitting for the Hare’s brightest star. This yellow-white **supergiant** shines about 27,000 times brighter than the Sun.

23685.fact: An orange giant **40 times wider** than the Sun, about 213 light-years away. Its outer layers slowly **pulse** in and out.

27288.fact: In 2001 astronomers confirmed it has an **asteroid belt**. In 2026 it was named Darlugal, from the Sumerian name for this constellation, **“the Rooster”**.

28103.fact: A yellow-white star about **49 light-years** away. The Spitzer space telescope found a **dusty disc** spreading out around it.

24845.fact: A **runaway star**, racing away from its birthplace among Orion’s young stars. It’s a hot blue star about 15 times the Sun’s mass.

28910.fact: About **1.6 million years ago** it passed within 29 light-years of the Sun. It’s a fast-spinning white star that **bulges** at its middle.

73273.fact: A hot blue giant near the end of its hydrogen-burning life. At almost 9 times the Sun’s mass, it may one day **explode** as a supernova.

75141.fact: A hot blue-white star about **12 times the Sun’s mass**, spinning fast. Its brightness quivers slightly because it gently **pulses**.

74395.fact: An orange giant with a fainter **golden-yellow partner** that a small telescope shows nearby. They sit about 117 light-years away.

75177.fact: An orange giant **40 times wider** than the Sun, about 275 light-years away. It’s heading toward us at about 29 km per second.

78918.fact: Spinning at around 330 km per second, it **bulges** 15% at its middle. It’s only about **25 million years old**, about 410 light-years away.

76705.fact: In about **2.8 million years** it will pass within 36 light-years of us. It’s a yellow giant wrapped in a cold shell of gas.

45688.fact: A telescope shows a blue-white star with a fainter companion some call **lilac**. That companion is really two stars, circling every 2.1 years.

41075.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the thorn”**. This orange giant is about **53 times wider** than the Sun and gently changes in brightness.

30060.fact: Two stars circling each other every **3.6 years**. They probably **eclipse** each other, dimming the light for a while.

91262.fact: About **14,000 years ago** it was the North Star, and it will be again around the year 13,700. It was the first star besides the Sun to be **photographed**.

92420.fact: Two stars so close that gas **pours** from one onto the other. They eclipse each other every **12.9 days**, a change you can follow by eye.

91971.fact: In 2026 it was named **Kautoki**, “the adze handle”, from a star picture used on the Pacific island of **Kapingamarangi**.

29271.fact: The **faintest “brightest star”** of any constellation. It’s named Hoerikwaggo, after **Table Mountain** in South Africa, which gave Mensa its name.

103738.fact: The brightest star of the **Microscope**, yet too faint to see from city skies. It’s a yellow giant about 223 light-years away.

105382.fact: Patches of odd metals like **strontium and europium** dot its surface, so its brightness flickers as it turns, every 2.1 days.

30867.fact: **William Herschel** called it “one of the most beautiful sights in the heavens”. A telescope shows **three blue stars** in a curved line.

29651.fact: An orange giant about 51 times wider than the Sun. Its **white dwarf** partner once sprinkled it with **barium**.

39863.fact: A yellow **supergiant** about 2,200 times brighter than the Sun. Its light set out roughly 1,000 years ago.

31216.fact: A white **supergiant** wrapped in a small glowing dust cloud, sitting between the **Rosette Nebula** and the Christmas Tree Cluster.

31978.fact: The brightest star of the **Christmas Tree Cluster**. Its main star is a scorching blue star, around **30 to 40 times** the Sun’s mass.

62322.fact: Two similar blue-white stars that circle each other every **194 years**, about 340 light-years away.

57363.fact: It marks the **tail of the Fly**. It’s really **three stars**, about 128 light-years away.

59929.fact: A red giant **116 times wider** than the Sun. It’s racing through space at about 100 km per second, much faster than its neighbours.

80582.fact: Named Yaqana, the **llama**, after an Inca constellation made of dark dust clouds. Its two inner stars circle each other every 3.3 days.

78914.fact: A white star with unusual metals in its light. The way it drifts across the sky hints at a **hidden partner**.

112405.fact: A white star in Octans, the constellation that holds the **south pole of the sky**. Its motion hints at an unseen partner.

86032.fact: Its name means **“head of the serpent collector”**, marking Ophiuchus’s head. It has a partner star that circles it every **8.6 years**.

81377.fact: The **nearest O-type star**, a blazing blue giant **ploughing** through dust clouds and pushing up a glowing bow wave.

86742.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the shepherd’s dog”**. This orange giant is about 12 times wider than the Sun, about 83 light-years away.

79882.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“hand”**. With Yed Prior, it marks the hand of Ophiuchus that **grips the serpent’s head**.

88048.fact: An orange giant with **two brown dwarfs** circling it. They move in step, which hints they formed like planets in a disc around the star.

80883.fact: Its name means **“elbow”** in Arabic. It’s really **four stars**, about 173 light-years away.

85423.fact: It used to be called **Theta Telescopii**, before the borders moved it into Ophiuchus. It’s a yellow-white star about 112 light-years away.

80343.fact: An orange giant about 11 times wider than the Sun, now burning **helium** in its core. It sits right by Ophiuchus’s border with Scorpius.

100751.fact: Britain’s Royal Air Force needed a name for it in the late 1930s for a **navigation** guide, so it was simply called **Peacock**, after Pavo.

99240.fact: A Sun-like star just **20 light-years** away, a bit older than the Sun. In about 49,000 years it will pass within 18 light-years of us.

98495.fact: A young white star, only about **27 million years old**, about 105 light-years away. It travels with a family of young stars.

105858.fact: A Sun-like star just **30 light-years** away, with fewer metals than the Sun. It was on a NASA list of top places to search for **rocky planets**.

88866.fact: A white giant with odd amounts of **strontium**, paired with a small orange dwarf. They sit about 130 light-years away.

107315.fact: Its name means **“nose”** in Arabic, marking the winged horse’s muzzle. This orange supergiant is about **183 times wider** than the Sun.

113963.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the saddle”**. It’s one corner of the **Great Square** of Pegasus.

112158.fact: Its name means **“lucky star of rain”** in Arabic. It’s a yellow bright giant with a partner that circles it every 813 days.

112748.fact: Its Arabic name means **“lucky star of the splendid one”**. It’s a yellow giant about 113 light-years away, bright enough to spot on a **moonlit night**.

109176.fact: Two very **young** Sun-like stars circling each other every **10 days**, just 38 light-years away.

107354.fact: Three stars in one: a pair circling every **11.6 years**, and one of those is itself two stars orbiting every **six days**.

109410.fact: A yellow-white giant spinning unusually fast for its age. It drifts through space with the **Big Dipper’s family** of stars, way out on the edge.

14576.fact: The **Demon Star**: every 2.9 days it fades to about a third of its brightness for some 10 hours, as a dimmer partner **eclipses** it.

18532.fact: A hot blue giant about **28,000 times brighter** than the Sun. A smaller partner swings around it every 14 days.

17358.fact: Part of the **Segment of Perseus**, a curve of stars across the hero. It’s a fast-spinning blue-white giant about 520 light-years away.

17529.fact: A yellow-white bright giant about **600 times brighter** than the Sun and 21 times wider. It’s roughly 560 light-years away.

14668.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“wrist”**. It’s really **three stars**, about 113 light-years away.

13531.fact: Two stars that **eclipse** each other only once every **4.15 years**, very slow for an eclipsing pair. One eclipse was carefully watched in 1989.

18614.fact: A scorching blue **O-type giant**, about 1,200 light-years away. Its fierce light makes the nearby **California Nebula** glow.

14632.fact: A Sun-like star just **34.5 light-years** away, a little bigger and about twice as bright as our Sun.

19812.fact: A yellow **supergiant** with a partner that circles it every 284 days. About 5.6 million years ago it passed closer and looked brighter.

16826.fact: A **Be star** wearing a disc of gas about 11 times its own width around its middle. Its brightness shifts slightly as a result.

13879.fact: Named for the **second of the three Gorgons** in the Perseus myth. It’s a fast-spinning white star about 303 light-years away.

5165.fact: Two matching yellow giants that circle each other every **171 years**, about 182 light-years away.

765.fact: An orange giant 10 times wider than the Sun, now burning **helium** in its core. It’s about 144 light-years away.

5348.fact: Two stars that **eclipse** each other every 1.67 days, so it fades noticeably by eye. The system probably holds **four stars** in all.

27321.fact: Just **23 million years old**, it’s ringed by a huge dusty disc and **three planets**, all photographed directly.

113368.fact: Its name means **“mouth of the fish”** in Arabic. Rings of **debris** circle it, and what looked like a planet there now seems to be dust from a huge crash.

113246.fact: A yellow giant with a **faint partner star** right beside it, a pair you need a telescope to split. They sit about 172 light-years away.

107380.fact: A blue-white star about 200 light-years away. As it circles the Milky Way, it swings between about **18,000 and 24,000 light-years** from the centre.

109285.fact: Spinning at about 308 km per second, it **bulges** 23% wider at its middle. It gives off X-rays that might come from a **hidden partner**.

35264.fact: An orange **supergiant** about **235 times wider** than the Sun, roughly 810 light-years away. It’s only about 20 million years old.

38170.fact: A yellow supergiant about **124 times wider** than the Sun, part of a family of **three stars** about 1,200 light-years away.

37677.fact: A very rare kind of supergiant wrapped in a **disc of dust**. A small partner star is passing gas to it, about 2,000 light-years away.

38070.fact: A fast-spinning **Be star** with a likely tiny, stripped-down partner. Its light changes every **28.9 days** as they orbit.

42828.fact: The brightest star of the **Compass**. With over 10 times the Sun’s mass, it will probably end its life as a **supernova**.

43409.fact: An orange giant nearly 22 times wider than the Sun, roughly **four billion years old**. It’s about 207 light-years away.

17440.fact: An orange giant with a small **red dwarf** partner that circles it every **5.25 years**. They’re about 101 light-years away.

18597.fact: A cool red giant about **56 times wider** than the Sun, glowing about 1,100 times brighter. It’s roughly 530 light-years away.

97365.fact: A **red giant** 180 times wider than the Sun, paired with a hot blue-white star. They circle each other about every **10 years**.

96837.fact: Named Shakh in 2026, after the ancient Sumerian star figure of **the pig**. It may have marked the **pig’s nose**.

116231.fact: A **mercury-manganese star**, with extra mercury, manganese and silicon showing in its light. It sits about 174 light-years away.

117452.fact: **Three stars** in one: a white star, a faint close partner, and a yellow star farther out. They’re about 137 light-years away.

92175.fact: A yellow bright giant about **49 times wider** than the Sun, with a hot blue-white partner that circles it every 2.3 years.

91726.fact: The star that gave its name to a whole family of pulsing stars, the **Delta Scuti variables**. It brightens and dims every **4.65 hours**.

77233.fact: It sits in the **Serpent’s head**. It spins so fast that it’s about 4.2 Suns wide at its middle but only 3.1 from pole to pole.

76276.fact: **Three stars** in the Serpent’s head. The brightest pulses every 3.7 hours, and the whole system is heading our way.

77450.fact: A red giant about **71 times wider** than the Sun, in the Serpent’s head. It’s moving toward us at about 38 km per second.

49641.fact: The **equator star**: it sits just south of the sky’s equator, and it crossed over from the north side in **December 1923**.

90422.fact: Ptolemy counted it in the **Southern Crown**, but in the 1700s Lacaille moved it into his new constellation, the **Telescope**.

89112.fact: An orange giant about 20 times wider than the Sun, with a disc of **dust** circling it. It’s about 410 light-years away.

8796.fact: Its name means **“the head of the triangle”**. It’s a yellow-white star stretched into an egg shape by a close **red dwarf** partner.

82273.fact: The brightest corner of the **Southern Triangle**. This orange giant is about **139 times wider** than the Sun, roughly 391 light-years away.

74946.fact: One corner of the **Southern Triangle**. It’s a white giant spinning unusually fast, about 190 light-years away.

114996.fact: It marks the **toucan’s beak**. It’s a yellow-white star about 75 light-years away that may have a hidden partner.

2484.fact: Part of a group of **six stars** loosely bound together, about 140 light-years away. Three are bright enough to get their own Greek letters.

110838.fact: A fast-spinning blue-white star with a **yellow partner** right beside it, a pair a small telescope can split. They’re about 250 light-years away.

50801.fact: Its name comes from an Arabic phrase for **“the second spring of the gazelle”**, a leap marked by pairs of stars. It’s a red giant **75 times wider** than the Sun.

46853.fact: A yellow-white star just **44 light-years** away. Astronomers have argued since 1976 about whether it has a **hidden partner**.

50372.fact: With Tania Australis, it marks one of the gazelle’s leaps, a pair of stars under the Great Bear’s paws. It’s a white star about **138 light-years** away.

44471.fact: Its name comes from the Arabic for **“the leap”** of a gazelle. It’s really two white stars, about 358 light-years away.

57399.fact: Its Chinese name means **“Guard of the Sun”**. It’s an orange giant 23 times wider than the Sun, about 198 light-years away.

55203.fact: The **first double star** ever to have its orbit worked out, back in 1828. It’s really **five stars**, just 28.5 light-years away.

44816.fact: Suhail is a common Arabic boy’s name once given to several bright southern stars. This orange supergiant is about **211 times wider** than the Sun.

52727.fact: Two stars on a wildly **stretched orbit**. Every 138 years they swing from about 100 times Earth’s distance from the Sun to just 3.

46651.fact: Two yellow-white stars that circle each other every **34 years**, just 61 light-years away.

41312.fact: An orange giant whose mass was measured by studying its **“starquakes”**, tiny ripples on its surface. It’s about 107 light-years away.

35228.fact: A yellow bright giant about 36 times wider than the Sun and over **a thousand times brighter**. It sits about 740 light-years away.

39794.fact: It sits in the middle of the **Flying Fish**, joining its wings. It’s really **four stars**, in two close pairs.

99874.fact: **Three stars** in one. The main orange giant and its closest partner circle each other every **25 years**, about 327 light-years away.

98543.fact: A white star with unusual **metal lines** in its light, now starting to grow older and bigger. It’s about 243 light-years away and heading toward us.
